_voice: Polite "ເຈົ້າ", warm standard Lao.
_style: Address the user politely as “ເຈົ້າ” (never ມຶງ/ໂຕ/ນາງ/ທ້າວ); the couple together is “ເຈົ້າທັງສອງ” or “ທັງສອງ”, and in the couple’s own voice “ພວກເຮົາ”/“ຂອງເຮົາ” (e.g. “ຕົ້ນໄມ້ຂອງພວກເຮົາ”). The other person is always “ຄູ່ຂອງເຈົ້າ” (short form “ຄູ່”), never ແຟນ/ຜົວ/ເມຍ/ສາມີ/ພັນລະຍາ, and never gendered words such as ລາວຜູ້ຊາຍ, ນາງ, ທ້າວ; if a pronoun is needed use the neutral “ລາວ” or simply repeat “ຄູ່ຂອງເຈົ້າ”. Keep sentences gender-neutral; do not add ຄັບ/ຄ່ະ/ເດີ to UI text (they mark the speaker’s gender or sound chatty) — warmth comes from wording like “ນຳກັນ”, “ແດ່”, “ເນາະ” used sparingly in friendly messages only. Quotes are curly “ ” with inner ‘ ’; ellipsis is the single character “…”. Lao script has no spaces between words: put a single space only between phrases/clauses and around Latin words, numbers and placeholders (e.g. “%lld ມື້”, “ເປີດວັນທີ %@”); do not end short labels with a full stop, and in sentences the Western period is optional and usually omitted — keep ! ? only where the English has them, with no space before them; keep “ · ” separators and \n exactly. Use Western digits 0–9 (not ໐–໙), dates day-month-year with Lao month names (ມັງກອນ … ທັນວາ) and Gregorian years, 24-hour time. Lao has no capitals: keep Latin brand words as written (Coupley, Premium, AI, CoupleSync) and keep buttons short verbs or verb phrases without ກະລຸນາ (“ບັນທຶກ”, “ຜະນຶກຈົດໝາຍ”, “ລອງໃໝ່”); use ກະລຸນາ only in longer instructional sentences when really needed. Plural category is only ["other"]: one form with the number, no plural marker (“%lld ມື້”, never ມື້ໆ). A partner’s name placeholder (%@) is never modified or attached to particles that would change it; rephrase so it stands alone (e.g. “ຂໍ້ຄວາມຈາກ %@”). Tone: warm, light, kind standard Vientiane Lao, natural rather than word-for-word, never cheesy.
